clue.text: New tails jaunty editor wore as experiment

indicators.note: to tail is to follow behind, so the abbreviation for new comes after the anagram
jaunty suggests something tossed about lightly, so the letters of editor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor sports a jaunty new set of tails, trying out a new look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaunty' rearranges the letters of editor, and 'tails' puts the new abbreviation after them.
explanation.definitionFit: To try a garment on is to wear it briefly as a test before buying.

clue.text: To amuse unruly heirs I've to play 12, say

parts.note: to tickle someone is to amuse them

indicators.note: unruly letters will not stay in line, so heirs I've to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent tries to entertain some badly behaved heirs by playing a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges HEIRSIVETO into THE IVORIES. 12 is the piano piece Chopsticks, which is played on the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were once made of elephant tusk, so the idiom means playing the piano, for instance a simple tune.

clue.text: See 1
Jot down sentence? On the contrary

indicators.note: the contrary of a word is it turned the other way, so the word for a sentence is read backwards

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence (from birdlime, rhyming slang for time)

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a sentence down, then a quibble suggesting the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down sentence' tempts a solver to write BIRD downwards; 'On the contrary' says read it the other way. BIRD is British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A drib is a small amount, as in dribs and drabs, just as a jot is a tiny bit.

clue.text: Diminutive hard case headbutts man over £50

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces sit above the later ones

parts.note: to nut someone is British slang for headbutting them
he is a pronoun for a man
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A tough guy headbutts a man for more than fifty quid.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hard case' is a tough person on the surface, but here it is the shell of a nut; 'Diminutive' points to 'in a nutshell', meaning in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: The shell of a nut is a small, hard casing, and the word also stands for anything put concisely.

clue.text: In England, where Geordies are law-abiding

definitions.meaning: Geordies come from Newcastle, up north and over to the right on a map of England

explanation.surface: A claim that the people of north-east England keep to the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle upon Tyne, which sits at the top right of a map of England: 'up right'. 5 is also a kind of piano, which matters to 6-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally upright people are honest and respectable, keeping to the rules.

clue.text: Recycled urine bottles 'pee green'

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so one piece is held inside the other
recycled material is processed into a new form, so the letters of urine are rearranged

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: A grim scene of recycled urine stored in bottles with a greenish label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' rearranges URINE into UNRIE, and 'bottles' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is not yet ripe, so green and not ripe are synonyms.

clue.text: Man Friday that usually has the 24 on 5 or 10

definitions.meaning: a loyal assistant, after Crusoe's servant; one's trusted second, as in the phrase with man

definitions.text: that usually has the 24 on 5 or 10
definitions.meaning: on an upright or grand piano, the melody is normally played by one particular hand

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe's servant is credited with carrying a melody on a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is TUNE, 5 is UPRIGHT and 10 is GRAND, both kinds of piano. A Man Friday is a trusted helper, a 'right-hand man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a chief assistant, and at the keyboard the right hand normally carries the melody.

clue.text: Galahad, disembowelled, claims his weapon took a deflection

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the outer letters enclose the weapon
with the insides removed, only the first and last letters of Galahad remain

parts.note: a knight such as Galahad fights with a lance

explanation.surface: Sir Galahad, gutted in battle, says his lance was turned aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disembowelled' keeps only the first and last letters of Galahad, and 'claims' wraps them round the knight's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow that glances off something strikes at an angle and is deflected.

clue.text: Changes in level, i.e. bottom to top

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom letter is the last, and it is taken up to the start

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A note explaining that changes in level run from the bottom upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom to top' takes the T at the end of IDEST, the Latin behind 'i.e.', and moves it to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's regular rise and fall alters the water level along a coast twice a day.

clue.text: Getting round in, S. Richter ordered a treble, perhaps

indicators.note: in signals one piece going inside the other
ordered letters are put into a new arrangement, so S. Richter is rearranged

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: The pianist Sviatoslav Richter, buying drinks, orders a round of trebles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges SRICHTER, and 'Getting round in' puts O inside. A 'treble' tempts as a triple drink; it is a boy soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singer with a high voice, typically one of the members of a church choir.

clue.text: Luxurious German marque fails to start

indicators.note: a word that fails to start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand of car

explanation.surface: An upmarket German car brand that will not start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' drops the first letter of the word for a marque.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand is magnificent and lavish, so it is a synonym for luxurious.

clue.text: Contents of old jar — bird's nest?

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, here taken from each of three words

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bird's nest inside an old jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' takes the middle of each of old, jar and bird: L, A and IR. The question mark warns that the nest belongs to an animal, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den or home is a sort of nest for it, a place it shelters and rears young.

clue.text: Tricky utensils for eating seconds of cutlet

parts.note: a cutlet is a chop, here plural as cuts of meat
ticks of the clock are seconds

explanation.surface: A diner struggling with awkward cutlery over a second helping of cutlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' tempts as second helpings; it is TICKS. The answer is also a simple piano tune, which 1-down needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of thin sticks used for eating in East Asia take practice, hence tricky.

clue.text: Examine lice jumping around in seed store

parts.note: to test something is to examine it

indicators.note: letters jumping around are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a patient for lice hopping about the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping around' rearranges the letters of lice; 'seed store' is a cheeky anatomical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The male gland that produces and holds sperm is, figuratively, a store of seed.

clue.text: Sentinel a stickler at heart, refusing to bend

indicators.note: at the heart of these words, running across them, the answer sits inside

explanation.surface: A guard who is a stickler for rules will not compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: A material that cannot stretch or flex lacks elasticity, so it will not give or bend.

clue.text: Firm in profit short of cash

parts.note: firm means hard, solid
to be up is to be ahead or in profit

explanation.surface: A company that is profitable on paper still lacks ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone poor, lacking money, so it matches being short of funds.

clue.text: Stubborn as a mule led by a brute

indicators.note: led by puts the leader first, so the brute comes before

parts.note: a pig is a brute or boorish person
headed means led

explanation.surface: A mule plodding behind a brutish handler, both obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by a brute' read literally is headed by a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate people are compared to mules; this word means just as obstinate.

clue.text: Without touching the ground, six leap over a train line

indicators.note: in a down clue the leap sits over, above, the later pieces

parts.note: to bound is to leap
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone leaps right over a railway line without landing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball hit over the rope at the edge of the field without bouncing scores six runs, called a six or a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket shot that clears the rope on the full is the six-run hit, the top-scoring stroke.

clue.text: Dub in Spanish the hardest part of 2

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
to dub is to name

explanation.surface: A film dubbed into Spanish, with a mention of something very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the word for dub inside the Spanish article. 2 is IVORIES, slang for teeth, whose outer coating is the hardest tissue in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The coating of teeth is the hardest substance in the human body.

clue.text: Spray cold contents on a painful back

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the earlier pieces sit above
back means read in the reverse direction

parts.note: sore means painful

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters

explanation.surface: A cold spray applied to an aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for painful round, giving EROS; 'contents' takes the inner letters of cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can that releases a fine mist is a spray.

clue.text: Heavy metal composer, blogger excited about date, or mountain as 3 set by Bach?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the date goes inside
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the clue gives three alternative routes to the first word, so it supplies three variations

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy metal composer and an excited blogger, before Bach's famous set.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers three routes to the first word: heavy metal plus a composer, the blogger anagram round D, or heavy metal plus a mountain. 'as 3' calls these variations; 'about' puts D inside GOLBERG, the anagram from 'excited'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach's keyboard work of thirty variations on an aria is named after the harpsichordist who supposedly played it.

clue.text: Fast Australian runner behind rival

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird that runs fast
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A fast Australian sprinter trails behind a competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian runner' looks like an athlete; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or surpass them, as a rival does.

clue.text: Bell's major feature of Scotch scene

parts.note: big means major
a ben is a Scottish mountain

explanation.surface: A whisky maker's main selling point is a Highland landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Bell's is a brand of Scotch whisky, which pulls toward drink. A ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: The great hour bell in the Elizabeth Tower at Westminster in London carries that nickname.

clue.text: See 20
Where streams flow after five beers

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Beer flowing freely after five pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Valleys are the low ground where rivers and streams run.

clue.text: See pitch isn't flat before starting to play

definitions.text: See pitch isn't flat before starting to play

parts.words: See pitch isn't flat before starting to play
parts.note: a musician adjusts an instrument so that its notes are true before beginning

explanation.surface: Advice to a musician to check their instrument before a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust an instrument's strings so the notes sound true is the verb, done before playing.

clue.text: Novel — one of many covered by English degree

indicators.note: covered by means held inside

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: one of the letters of many, its first

explanation.surface: A novel that is one of many on an English degree reading list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of many' gives M, and 'covered by' puts it inside E and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote a novel of that name about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: See 27
Tight underwear? Assistant grabs M&S catalogue for discussion

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

indicators.note: to grab is to seize, so the assistant holds the store's initials

parts.note: a hand is a helper or assistant
the initials of Marks & Spencer, a British store chain

indicators.note: for discussion means as spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A shop assistant picks up a Marks & Spencer catalogue to discuss tight underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Cockney rhyming slang for drunk. M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street chain; 'grabs' puts MS in HAND, and 'for discussion' gives a word said like LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and the two composers' names rhyme with a coarse British word for drunk.

clue.text: Is Nico confused about Latin? Si

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the letter
confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muddled about Latin answers yes in Spanish or Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Si' looks like a foreign yes; it is the chemical symbol. 'confused' gives SIICON, and 'about' puts L in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Si is the chemical symbol for the element, atomic number fourteen.

clue.text: Did long negotiation initially set back financial deadline?

indicators.note: set back means moved further toward the end of the word

parts.note: yearned means longed, did long

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of negotiation

explanation.surface: A drawn-out negotiation delayed the accounts deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives N, and 'set back' moves the N in YEARNED one place later.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies close their accounts at the end of the financial year, a fixed reporting deadline.
